raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame regardless of the destination lookup outcome — learning (wire → learn) occurs before, and independently of, the destination lookup (lookup → hit) in the flow.
A2: It associates the source MAC address (SA) with the ingress port on which the frame arrived.
A3: Whether the destination MAC address has an entry found in the MAC table ("Entry found?") — if yes it forwards out the single learned port, if no it floods.
A4: It floods the frame to all ports in the VLAN; the ingress port is always excluded.
A5: NOT STATED
A6: When the destination's egress port is the same as the ingress port, the switch filters (drops) the frame instead of sending it out any port.
A7: Once the station's port is learned, frames addressed to it are forwarded out only that single learned port (unless that port equals the ingress port, in which case the frame is filtered), rather than being flooded to all ports.
A8: NOT STATED
